== Tournament Results audit and lead photo (October 2026) ==
Checked against every wiki page that names him, the Players Committee forum and site search, DeckTech reports and Decipher's 1997–2001 pages. Added:
* [[February 1997 St. Louis tournament]], 4th of 32, from Decipher's NewsFlash ([https://web.archive.org/web/19970327231956/http://rothko.decipher.com:80/newsandhighlights/stlouistournament.html Preserved copy]). The report gives "2/23" with no year; the capture is from March 1997 and names "March 23, a Sunday" as the next event, so 23 February 1997.
* [[2000 Death Star II Pre-Release (Normal)]], 8th of 90 with 6 (+52), from the organizer's forum post ([https://web.archive.org/web/20261027125252/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t8037-start40.html Preserved copy]). The post dates the event 6/26/2000. Three DeckTech reports and the event page give 24 June 2000, which the row keeps. The post also lists a "Cabe Cummins" 2nd (8 (+51), Dark); the event page has [[Kade Cummins]].
* [[2000 Origins Team Event]] (teammate of [[Geoff Snider]]) and [[2001 Wizard World Episode I Closed Environment tournament]] (Snider's game 4 opponent, Light "Shmi's Hut podracing"). Neither report gives his finish.
* [[2001 Normal DPC]] Light deck "Profit/Harvest", from [[Steve Kuperman]]'s DeckTech deck notes (game 1 opponent).

Not added, as the sources do not show he played or what he placed:
* [[2001 Wizard World King of Corellia]]: Bradley Augsburger's report says "Olson and Greg Heisler show up, and we get started".
* Michael Girard's DeckTech report thanks "Greg Heisler - for the Icebox and the Icebox II - The Wicked in Wisconsin"; this could mean he ran those events.

Lead photo: [[:File:Greg Heisler DecipherCon 1999.jpg]], cropped from Decipher's sat54 photo, whose caption names "Greg Heisler and Matt Reed". The left man matches Decipher's named "Go Greg Heisler!" photo and his ''Star Wars Insider'' #48 card, and the right man matches [[Matthew Reed]]'s card. The uncropped photo is in == Photographs ==. The Players Committee site search had no hits for "heisler". YouTube and Facebook were not searched, because Decipher's own photos named him.
